problem: Existing environment acoustic modeling methods (neural fields, FS-RIR, Mesh2IR) need dense RIR collection or privileged floorplan/mesh knowledge and assume instant access to arbitrary positions, which is unrealistic for a robot exploring an unmapped scene.
motivation: Acoustic models matter for robotics (audio-based navigation, source separation) and AR/MR spatialization, but capturing RIRs is slow and intrusive. A mobile agent should therefore decide where to move and where to sample with a small sample budget, and the best acoustic sampling spots differ from those that maximize floorplan coverage.
key_idea: Train an RL policy that navigates an unmapped scene and decides when to sample audio-visual observations, using a reward based on global improvement of a frozen acoustic rendering model's RIR prediction error.
insight: The global acoustic-improvement reward gives the best error (8.08e-3), better than local acoustic reward (8.11), coverage/novelty-only rewards (8.11-8.15) and uniform sampling with the same reward (8.24), so both the acoustic signal and the active choice of when to sample matter. Qualitatively, the agent samples in acoustically changing areas such as winding hallways and avoids redundant views. However, gaps among ablations are small (about 0.03-0.16e-3), while the gain over naive baselines is large.
method: Task formulation: active acoustic sampling with navigation budget T=200 and sample budget N=20; actions are {Forward, TurnLeft, TurnRight}x{Sample, Skip}, and the sampling decision is made before capturing audio.

Policy inputs/architecture: ResNet encoders for RGB + cumulative top-down occupancy map and for the previous binaural echo spectrogram, sinusoidal pose embedding, concatenated and fed to an RNN with an actor-critic head.
Acoustic prediction reward: r^A_t = L^R_{t-1} - L^R_t, the drop in mean L1 RIR spectrogram error over K fixed global query poses, given only on Sample steps.

Auxiliary dense rewards: area-coverage reward (relative increase) and count-based novelty reward 1/sqrt(n(m_t)) on 1x1 m grid cells, with weights 2e5 (acoustic), 2e2 (coverage), 10 (novelty); trained with DD-PPO.

Acoustic rendering model: FS-RIR (transformer encoder-decoder) pre-trained disembodied with random context, then frozen during RL for reward stationarity; policy is renderer-agnostic (also tested with NAF).

setting.backbone: ResNet audio/visual encoders + RNN actor-critic policy (trained with DD-PPO); frozen FS-RIR transformer as rendering model
setting.training_data: 56 MP3D training scenes in SoundSpaces 2.0; 150K PPO iterations; FS-RIR pre-trained on random-sampled context
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (90° FoV), binaural echo response (when sampled), camera pose, accumulated top-down occupancy map
setting.privileged: none at test time (pose given; GT RIRs used only for training reward)

numbers.eval_set_note: 12 unseen test scenes, 225 episodes, 60 query poses per scene
numbers.backbone: ResNet+RNN policy with frozen FS-RIR renderer
numbers.extra: T=200, N=20; STFT error in base 1e-3

numbers.backbone: ResNet+RNN policy with frozen FS-RIR renderer
numbers.extra: passive sampling every T/N steps; STFT in base 1e-3

numbers.backbone: ResNet+RNN policy with frozen FS-RIR renderer
numbers.extra: local acoustic reward variant; STFT in base 1e-3

numbers_note: Custom task/metric (STFT L1 error, lower better); SOTA comparison with FS-RIR and NAF given only in figures. Text says FS-RIR needs 86 samples to match ActiveRIR's error with 20.
results: ActiveRIR reaches STFT error 8.08e-3 on unseen scenes vs Random 13.04, Greedy 14.46 and Forward 14.68. It matches passive uniform sampling's quality in >70% fewer steps, and beats FS-RIR with floorplan-based random sampling, which needs 86 samples to match its 20.
limitations: Small margins over ablations (e.g., 8.08 vs 8.11-8.24), with no variance or significance reported
Simulation only, with discrete 1 m/90° actions and pose available; noise robustness tested only with Gaussian noise
Random sampling from floorplan may outperform ActiveRIR in high-resource regimes; restricted to a single 2D-receiver setup
